newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Dlr/mark vols jump, dlr/yen curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Dlr/mark vols jump, dlr/yen curve steepens.

text.p: A sharp fall in spot dollar/mark pushed option implied volatilities higher in late morning U.S., despite the weekend time-decay factor, dealers said.
The dollar tumbled more than half a pfennig to below 1.5180 marks on Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's remarks that he saw no need for further interest rate cuts in the foreseeable future.
"Front-end got bid immediately," said a U.S. bank trader in New York, adding that dealers had already been wary of going short in volatilities after a steady rise this week.
One-month dollar/mark volatility rose about 0.2 point from European midsession levels to 6.9/7.2 percent, roughly unchanged from late Thursday levels.
In a radio interview, Tietmeyer also said he saw a 1996 German economic growth of one percent or more and that nothing stood in the way of growth from an interest-rate point of view.
The mark's strength weighed on the dollar against the yen as well. Dollar/yen eased from its fresh 34-month-highs in the mid-113-yen area, relieving the upward pressure on yen implied volatilities.

"Spot has been grinding higher lately and that's been keeping options well bid," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York. "But the actual daily ranges haven't been spectacular, so there isn't as much bid in the front end as the back end because people don't really need gamma."

When the options market is driven by swings in the spot market, shorter-dated options are usually the most well bid because they have more gamma implications. But high-gamma positions are vulnerable to time decay in a slow spot market.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility was marginally above late Thursday levels at 7.0/7.2 percent. Six-month volatility stood at 8.75/8.85 percent and one-year at 9.3/9.4.
The one-month/one-year spread in dollar/yen of over two full percentage points sharply contrasts with below one point for an equivalent spread in dollar/mark.
Okada said longer-dated yen volatilities were supported by tight supply/demand and it was risky to go against the grain.
"You don't want to be short the back end and long the front end, even though the overall vega might seem decent," he said. Vega shows how premiums move per change in volatility.
Elsewhere, mark/yen volatilities also firmed, particularly the longer-dateds, as spot rose to fresh 3-1/2 year highs. Minutes after Tietmeyer's comments, one-year jumped 0.3 point to 7.1/7.3 percent.
Sterling volatilities were also buoyant as spot cable rose clearly past $1.6000. One-month cable volatility stood at 5.5/5.8 percent, a touch above late Thursday levels.
